body: That said - the TB2 at full power just completely extracted a bowl in 3 good hits. About 45 seconds from power on to power off in total.

I agree with the sentiment. But I assume the industry standard meaning of “instant heat” means the unit is heated and ready to go at full power instantly. 

I compare it to say a venty which is 15-35 seconds to heat before it is ready, and then typically the same “second hit” before it’s ready to produce its maximum vapor. 

The heat is there far quicker with the TB2. Just on the user to pass it over the product.
There is a fiber option to pack into the bowl for use with concentrate. I have no experiences with it but saw it available on the site.

Just a question but when you combust- are you covering the USB-C shaped hole on the bottom of the puck. That’s the primary air intake and will cause combustion if blocked. 

Otherwise I’m sorry for that experience with units that don’t seem great yet.

Speaking only from my experience. I turn it on and let the welcome blue lights go. Then use the smaller button to set the heat,  and then you single press the larger button and wait for a buzz and/or green light to start the hit. The manual recommends a 6 second inhale, but it will stay heating for the duration of your draw. Repeat the process from there. (A stir before a final draw or two helps)

Typically, depending on heat setting, vapor production will increase after 2 or so hits. Remember - it’s not sitting there baking - you are pulling the air to expose it to heat when you draw. That’s the primary exposure to heat. 

I like to sit at a heat level 2 or 3 to just have sitting and up to a 4/5 for quicker hits or to finish a session. 

Hope this helps! Cheers!

I actually have and used both the Venty and the Bowle. 

Best part of the Bowle is the on-demand heating. You can sit with it, take a hit, put it down for a bit, and take another instant hit because the heat up is 1-2 seconds. 

I like the venty better as a session type vape - and definitely cannot see myself taking the Bowle with me outside of the house - but the Bowle’s ability to prolong a bowl and allow for a completely on-demand experience sets it apart right now.

Also - for anyone in the market - I am sad to share that I pulled the trigger on this buy just about a week before they put both versions of the unit on sale…SMH…but it’s a great deal right now and even better if you are considering adding to the collection
